llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions generally match a local, code-first UI design workflow, but a prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md and the package includes executable Python scripts — review before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included assets: a large local design knowledge base (CSV data) and Python scripts for searching and generating design systems. No unrelated cloud credentials, system paths, or extra binaries are requested — the requested resources are proportionate to a local design/code workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to run local Python scripts (scripts/search.py, scripts/design_system.py, etc.) and read the included CSVs — that is coherent for this skill. However, static pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern inside SKILL.md (prompt-injection signal). Even though the visible SKILL.md content appears to be usage instructions, any prompt-injection content aimed at changing agent/system prompts or model behavior would be a high-risk escalation. Before running the skill, inspect SKILL.md and the scripts for any lines that attempt to override system prompts, embed hidden directives, or instruct sending data to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec that downloads remote artifacts; all files are present in the bundle. This is lower-risk than an installer that fetches code from an arbitrary URL. The only runtime action is executing included Python scripts locally, so risk comes from script contents rather than remote installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. That is proportional to the stated purpose. There is no evidence the skill expects unrelated secrets or cloud access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default model-invocation settings (agent can call it autonomously) are set. The skill does not request persistent system privileges or claim to modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is platform-normal; no extra persistence or privilege escalation is requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package mostly fits its description: local CSV knowledge plus Python scripts for generating and implementing design systems. However, before installing or running anything: 1) Open SKILL.md and search for any lines that try to override system prompts, inject instructions for the LLM beyond normal usage, or tell the agent to change its configuration — remove or refuse those. 2) Audit the Python scripts (scripts/*.py) for network calls, subprocess execution, or writing to arbitrary system paths — pay special attention to any requests.post/urllib/socket usage or calls to os.system/ subprocess. 3) Run the code in a sandboxed environment (isolated VM or container) if you want to execute the included scripts, and avoid exposing any secrets. 4) If you will let the agent invoke the skill autonomously, be cautious because a prompt-injection inside SKILL.md could cause it to alter model behavior; consider disabling autonomous invocation until you complete the audit. If you want, I can scan the scripts for network I/O or suspicious code patterns and highlight any lines that warrant deeper review.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: A prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md. Changing or overriding system prompts is unrelated to a UI design helper and is a potential attempt to manipulate model behavior. This may be a false positive (SKILL.md can contain meta/instructional text) but it should be manually reviewed.
